funds.name: Korea Fund of Funds (한국모태펀드 / Mother Fund)

strategy.thesis: Government-backed fund-of-funds operator. KVIC manages the Korea Fund of Funds (Mother Fund), seeding private venture capital partnerships rather than investing directly in startups, to provide a stable, market-driven supply of venture capital to Korean SMEs and ventures.

summary.en: Korea Venture Investment Corp (KVIC) is the government-owned professional operator of the Korea Fund of Funds (Mother Fund), established in 2005 under the Special Measures Act for Venture Business Development. It is a fund-of-funds: 13 government ministries/agencies contribute capital, KVIC invests into private venture capital partnerships, which in turn invest in startups and SMEs. The Mother Fund stood at about KRW 8.9 trillion at end-2023, and KVIC also runs the Smart Korea Fund and overseas global funds.
summary.local: 한국벤처투자(KVIC)는 2005년 설립된 정부 출자 모태펀드(한국모태펀드) 전담 운용기관으로, 13개 정부 부처·기관의 출자를 받아 민간 벤처투자조합에 출자하는 재간접(fund-of-funds) 구조로 운영된다. 2023년 말 기준 모태펀드 규모는 약 8조 8,968억 원이며, 스마트대한민국펀드와 해외진출 글로벌펀드도 운용한다.

name.en: Korea Institute of Startup & Entrepreneurship Development (KISED)

strategy.thesis: Central public agency under the Ministry of SMEs and Startups that designs and operates Korea's national startup-support programs (Pre-Startup Package, Startup Package, TIPS administration, K-Startup Grand Challenge, K-Startup portal, CCEI network), spanning education, commercialization grants and globalization.

program.eligibility: Korean and (for global programs) foreign founders / prospective founders depending on the specific program.

summary.en: KISED (Korea Institute of Startup & Entrepreneurship Development), established in 2008 and headquartered in Sejong, is the public institute under the Ministry of SMEs and Startups that runs Korea's flagship national startup programs. It administers the Pre-Startup Package, Startup Commercialization packages, the TIPS program (with KISED/MSS), the K-Startup Grand Challenge for foreign founders, the K-Startup portal, and the 17 Centers for Creative Economy & Innovation.

strategy.thesis: Government-funded agency under the Ministry of SMEs and Startups providing policy loans, direct lending, consulting, training, marketing and global-expansion support to Korean SMEs and startups; a primary channel for state policy finance rather than equity investment.

summary.en: KOSME (Korea SMEs and Startups Agency) is a non-profit, government-funded organization founded in 1979 under the Ministry of SMEs and Startups. It implements state SME/startup policy primarily through policy finance — direct loans, interest subsidies and consulting — rather than equity. For 2026 it finalized its SME & Startup Promotion Fund at KRW 11.5129 trillion, including KRW 4.0643 trillion in direct loans and KRW 367 billion in interest subsidies.

name.en: TIPS — Tech Incubator Program for Startup

strategy.thesis: Public-private partnership between the Ministry of SMEs and Startups and certified private operators (VCs/accelerators/successful founders). Selected operators make a private angel investment, which unlocks matching government R&D grants and commercialization support for technology startups.

investment.raw: Up to ~700M KRW per startup (100M angel investment + up to 500M R&D, expanding to 800M for deep tech); plus up to 400M additional investment and marketing support

program.eligibility: Early-stage technology startups selected via a certified TIPS operator (private investor) who first invests; standard, scale-up and global TIPS tracks.

summary.en: TIPS (Tech Incubator Program for Startup), launched in 2013, is Korea's flagship public-private deep-tech program run by the Ministry of SMEs and Startups and administered with KISED. A certified private operator (VC, accelerator or successful founder) first invests ~KRW 100M of angel capital into a startup, which then unlocks government matching R&D grants of up to KRW 500M (rising to KRW 800M for selected deep-tech), plus additional investment and marketing support. The grant is non-dilutive; startups repay only 10% as a 'loyalty' contribution on commercial success.
summary.local: TIPS(민간투자주도형 기술창업지원)는 2013년 시작된 중소벤처기업부의 대표 기술창업 지원 사업으로, KISED와 함께 운영된다. 민간 운영사(VC·액셀러레이터·성공창업가)가 약 1억 원의 엔젤투자를 선행하면 정부 R&D 자금(최대 5억 원, 딥테크는 8억 원까지 확대)과 추가 투자·마케팅 지원이 매칭된다. 지분을 받지 않으며 사업화 성공 시 R&D 자금의 10%만 환수한다.

strategy.thesis: Korea's flagship government accelerator for foreign startups, run by the Ministry of SMEs and Startups and KISED, to attract international founders to establish and scale operations in Korea via a hybrid acceleration program in English.

investment.raw: Settlement/commercialization funds plus prize money for top teams; up to ~USD 50,000 commercialization support cited; ~USD 55,000 non-dilutive funding cited for 2026

program.eligibility: Foreign nationals with prospective or existing startups established within seven years.

summary.en: The K-Startup Grand Challenge (KSGC), launched in 2016, is Korea's flagship government accelerator for foreign startups, run by the Ministry of SMEs and Startups and KISED. It attracts thousands of applications from 100+ countries; roughly 40 teams are selected per cycle (around 80 in some recent years) for a hybrid English-language incubation of about 3.5 months, with settlement funds, prize money for top teams, visa support and help establishing in Korea.
summary.local: K-Startup Grand Challenge(KSGC)는 2016년 시작된 외국인 창업가 대상 한국 대표 정부 액셀러레이터로, 중소벤처기업부와 창업진흥원(KISED)이 운영한다. 100여 개국에서 수천 건의 지원이 몰리며 매 회 약 40개 팀(최근 일부 회차는 약 80개)을 선발해 약 3.5개월의 영어 인큐베이션을 제공하고 정착자금·상금·창업비자·법인설립을 지원한다.

summary.en: The Centers for Creative Economy & Innovation (CCEI) are a nationwide network of 17 regional public innovation/incubation centers, established from 2014, each matched with a partner conglomerate and a specialized sector focus. Supported through KISED, they provide incubation space, mentoring, entrepreneurship education, startup contests, IR and globalization support to local founders, accelerating go-to-market in sectors such as fintech, gaming, healthcare/safety, IoT and 5G.

name.en: Global Digital Innovation Network (GDIN) — formerly Born2Global Centre

strategy.thesis: Government-funded global-expansion accelerator under the Ministry of Science and ICT, helping Korean tech startups scale internationally through consulting (legal, IP, visa, marketing), networking and investor connections; rebranded from Born2Global Centre to GDIN in 2024.

summary.en: Born2Global Centre — rebranded Global Digital Innovation Network (GDIN) in 2024 — is a government-funded accelerator under the Ministry of Science and ICT, established in 2013 and based at Pangyo. It supports Korean tech startups' global expansion through consulting (legal, IP, visa, marketing), networking and investor matching. It reports supporting 3,000+ companies, 20,000+ consulting cases, and attracting over USD 4 billion in investment, with member companies including unicorns Sendbird and Riiid and IPOs such as Lunit.
summary.local: 본투글로벌센터(Born2Global)는 2024년 글로벌디지털혁신네트워크(GDIN)로 명칭이 변경된 과학기술정보통신부 산하 정부 지원 액셀러레이터로, 2013년 설립되어 판교에 위치한다. 한국 테크 스타트업의 해외 진출을 위한 법률·IP·비자·마케팅 컨설팅, 네트워킹, 투자 연계를 지원하며, 3,000개 이상 기업 지원과 40억 달러 이상 투자 유치를 보고했다.

strategy.thesis: Government ICT-industry promotion agency under the Ministry of Science and ICT, supporting ICT startups and scale-ups through infrastructure, acceleration, mentoring and global-expansion programs; original organizer of the K-Startup Grand Challenge (2016).

summary.en: NIPA (National IT Industry Promotion Agency), established in 2009 under the Ministry of Science and ICT, is Korea's ICT-industry promotion agency. It supports ICT startups and scale-ups via infrastructure, acceleration, mentoring and global expansion, focusing on emerging technologies (AI, cloud, big data, IoT). NIPA originally launched and organized the K-Startup Grand Challenge in 2016.

strategy.thesis: State-owned Korea Development Bank's startup-ecosystem platform connecting startups with investors. NextRound runs IR/investor-matching events, NextONE provides early-stage acceleration with potential direct KDB investment, and NextRise is a large startup fair.

summary.en: Korea Development Bank (KDB), a state-owned policy bank, runs a startup-ecosystem platform via its NextRound Department: KDB NextRound (investor-matching IR events, launched 2016), KDB NextONE (early-stage acceleration with potential direct KDB investment) and NextRise (a large startup fair). Over its first 10 years, NextRound saw 1,026 of 3,339 participating companies secure investment — a 30.7% funding success rate — with cumulative investment reaching KRW 9.2 trillion.
summary.local: 한국산업은행(KDB)은 국책은행으로서 넥스트라운드 부서를 통해 창업 생태계 플랫폼을 운영한다. 투자자 매칭 IR인 KDB 넥스트라운드(2016년 시작), 초기 액셀러레이션과 직접투자가 가능한 KDB 넥스트원, 대형 창업박람회 넥스트라이즈로 구성된다. 출범 10년간 넥스트라운드 참여기업 3,339개 중 1,026개가 투자 유치(성공률 30.7%)했고 누적 투자액은 9조 2천억 원에 달한다.

summary.en: Seoul Business Agency (SBA) is the Seoul Metropolitan Government's SME and startup support institution, traced to a 1998 foundation and officially named SBA in 2005. It operates the Seoul Startup Hub, accelerating centers, and global/foreign business centers, providing workspace, incubation, mentoring, funding connections and international-expansion support. Seoul's wider plan targets fostering 50 unicorns by 2030.

strategy.thesis: Industry-backed fund-of-funds for the ICT sector. Funded by Korea's three telecom operators (SKT, KT, LG U+) and operated by the Korea Telecommunications Operators Association (KTOA), it invests into specialized venture funds backing promising IT/ICT ventures and SMEs.

summary.en: The Korea IT Fund (KIF), established in 2002, is an ICT-sector fund-of-funds created by Korea's three telecom operators (SKT, KT, LG U+) to support the IT industry. Operated by the Korea Telecommunications Operators Association (KTOA), it channels capital into specialized venture funds that invest in promising IT/ICT ventures and SMEs. The Ministry of Economy and Finance structured a first phase of US$100M in 2015 and renewed it for US$300M in 2017.
summary.local: 한국IT펀드(KIF)는 2002년 국내 3대 통신사(SKT·KT·LG U+)가 IT 산업 발전을 위해 조성한 ICT 분야 모태펀드로, 한국통신사업자연합회(KTOA)가 운용한다. 유망 IT/ICT 벤처·중소기업에 투자하는 전문 투자조합에 출자하며, 2015년 1억 달러 규모로 1단계가 구성된 뒤 2017년 3억 달러로 갱신되었다.
